args.name: weekly-sync
args.prompt: Weekly upstream sync for faker-kit. Goal: take the newest upstream commit without ever merging it myself. Step 1. Read the pinned ref with: gh api repos/acme/plugins/commits/main --jq .sha and compare it to the sha in upstream/source.json. If they match, stop and say nothing. Step 2. Read what changed with a read call: gh api repos/acme/plugins/compare/<ref>...<head> --jq '.files[].filename' and note any rule in upstream/model-map.json, upstream/compat-patches.json or upstream/renames.json whose count may change. Step 3. Start a cloud session for the sync: claude --cloud <session> -p 'Run node scripts/sync-upstream.mjs --ref <sha>, fix any rule whose count changed, read upstream/CHANGES.md in the diff, run the validate and kit-e2e checks, and open one ready pull request whose body starts with Unit: upstream-sync-weekly'. Step 4. Each wake, look at the pull request with faker-kit status. The pull request is never merged by this job and never merged by me: the owner merges it. Do not run faker-kit merge on it, do not call the merge API, and never force-push or push to main. Merge conflicts are fixed by merging origin/main into the branch. Step 5. When every check on the head passed, tell the owner the pull request is ready to merge, with the link, the head sha and the digests from both e2e runs. If a check failed, start a fresh cloud session on the same branch with the failure in its brief, at the next effort step up to high. Step 6. Keep the digest short: one line per pull request, no routine chatter, ping only when blocked, ready to merge, or done. Never read secrets, never edit the kit, and never write statuses, check runs, reviews or refs through the GitHub API. Extra care: the job only reads GitHub with gh api GET calls, so its prose may mention merge, merge API, statuses and check runs as things it must never write. If the compare shows more than 300 files, say so in one line and still open a single pull request. If the session cannot be started, report that once and try again on the next wake instead of starting a second session for the same ref. Remember: this job reads GitHub with gh api GET calls, starts sessions with claude --cloud, and hands the merge to the owner or to faker-kit merge when the owner asks.
